reason: Multi-agent code-generation eval system with a verification agent; reported claims are HumanEval pass rates ranking GPT-3.5/GPT-4/Bard, i.e. task outcomes, not the verification loop.
Multi-agent scientific corpus distillation framework; ablations validate each agent but the claims are downstream biomedical QA accuracy vs Med-PaLM-2 and GPT-4, not loop control.
Iterative resampling of variables from an LLM's conditionals is a Gibbs/MCMC sampler on a fixed schedule, not an autonomous agent's control loop.
BALAR is a task-agnostic outer loop whose iteration policy picks the next question by maximising expected mutual information and expands belief state; compared against reactive baselines.
The plan is refined offline from training error feedback; at test time the LLM does single-pass inference guided by the learned plan, so there is no runtime control loop.
STAgent is an agentic tool-using model built from a tool environment, data curation and an SFT/RL recipe; the reported claim is TravelBench and general-benchmark performance.
The agent explained is a robot with an uninterpretable deep network policy; the LLM only generates post-hoc explanations, so no language-model agent loop is studied.
A membership-inference evaluation over LMs trained on the Pile; no agent and no iterative control at all, only training-data leakage measurements.
Distillation pipeline compressing ReAct agents with span-specific losses; reported claims are ALFWorld/HotPotQA/WebShop scores and compression, not the loop the student runs.
xLAM contributes trained action models and a data pipeline; the evaluation is function-calling leaderboard performance, with no runtime loop mechanism as the contribution.
S-Agents proposes a tree-of-agents organisation but the evidence is only that it executes Minecraft building and resource collection; the topology is never the studied variable.
An overview paper summarising pretraining and fine-tuning data practices and listing open-source datasets; a secondary study with no method.
The iterative searching and ranking is a weight-sensitivity search for a bit-flip attack on model parameters, not an LLM agent's control loop.
KG-Agent's tool-select-then-update-memory iteration is the authors' own loop, but the reported claim is KGQA accuracy against larger LLMs on in- and out-domain datasets.
Hydrogen-Agent is a domain framework the authors built; claims are HydroBench factual accuracy over its base model and three end-to-end research case studies.
A systematisation that categorises runtime supply-chain threats into a taxonomy of data and tool attacks; a secondary study of the security literature.
A 33-task penetration-testing benchmark scored by success rate and task milestones; it measures task outcomes, not a loop property such as termination or retries.
The iteration is PPO plus Tabu Search over vehicle routes; the LLM only re-weights constraints, and results are distance, fuel and on-time delivery metrics.
ReaperAI is an offensive-security agent the authors built; the reported evidence is successful exploitation of known vulnerabilities on Hack The Box, a task outcome.
Self-described first comprehensive survey of LLM-based human-agent collaboration systems, with a paper list; a secondary study.
A survey of twenty-six LLM RTL-generation efforts plus a baseline benchmarking of frontier models; a secondary study, no loop mechanism contributed.
A review synthesising LangGraph, CrewAI and MCP multi-agent frameworks and their reported biomedical accuracies; a secondary study.
ARM is an RCA-plus-mitigation closed loop for cloud-edge faults; reported claims are 52.9% SLA-violation detection and 70.7% successful mitigation, i.e. task outcomes.
WaterRAG is a domain multi-agent RAG application; the ablation of its iterative loop is scored by 80.5% answer correctness on wastewater questions, a task outcome.
GENIUS's finite-state error-recovery machine is the studied retry/repair mechanism: 76.3% of failed runs are autonomously recovered, with attempt-wise success decaying exponentially.
ABA is an agentic auditing pipeline; the reported claims are that 25.7% of benchmark tasks have issues and that filtering shifts model rankings, not anything about its loop.
A Zenodo record written up from a YouTube video describing OpenClaw, with no method, evaluation or data; not a research contribution.
The loop architecture is the studied variable: one-shot vs iterative-feedback vs designer/debugger loops (only ~2pp gain vs ~20pp from model choice), plus five tool-calling agent designs.
Controlled longitudinal study holding the model fixed and varying only the agent harness over 35 releases, attributing quality shifts to the iteration policy and context handling it implements.
A conceptual taxonomy review distinguishing AI Agents from Agentic AI with application mapping and challenge analysis; a secondary study.
The curate-train-refine loop is a data-generation pipeline and the reported claim is classification accuracy over zero- and few-shot baselines on four benchmarks.
Position paper arguing explicitly about loop control: recasts the agent loop as a single-ready-unit scheduler and proposes an explicit DAG with a node state machine giving termination guarantees.
Zenith is a personal-assistant application; its PPAR loop and model router are evidenced only by 88% task success and 30% lower latency, i.e. task outcomes.

SafeAgent verifies each action around the agent loop and arbitrates whether it proceeds; ablations show recovery confidence and policy weighting set distinct safety-utility operating points.
The symbolic validator sits in the agent loop but the reported claims are requirements-task outputs: 100% coverage, 0.2% constraint violations and F1 0.47-0.51 against a gold standard.
A deployed Islamic assistant wiring a standard tool-using retrieval loop; the reported claims are exam scores, IslamicMMLU leaderboard position and deployment lessons.
The Actor-Critic-Distiller-Refiner loop serves a power-systems explanation application; the reported claim is ~96% on explanation quality metrics for OPF redispatch.
A survey of agent-harness components with a taxonomy, evaluation logic and model-harness coevolution discussion; a secondary study.
Compares iteration policies for vericoding: an agentic loop scaling with agent budget, then state-based vs context-based tree-search orchestrators against that baseline at lower token cost.
DIAFORGE is a synthesis-plus-finetuning pipeline; the live agentic loop is only the evaluation harness and the claim is tool-invocation success over GPT-4o and Claude-3.5.
Control topology is the studied variable: a capacity-limited selection and broadcast hub with diversity pruning, argued against unconstrained multi-agent loops to cut hallucination and add control.
Tests LLM-as-jury, the default stopping criterion for agent loops, as a verification mechanism on a legal gold set; finds systematic confident error and argues verification must be an external gate.
A podcast episode summary and show notes arguing against agentic inflation; not a research contribution.
A tutorial review mapping five enabling knowledge pillars for agentic biosensors onto a Knowledge Integration Framework; a secondary study.
